h1: Why SEO services matter more now, not less
metaTitle: Why SEO Services Are Important in 2026
metaDescription: Why SEO services matter now that AI answers absorb clicks: the pages cited by AI are the pages that already rank. Here's what that changes about your plan.
answer: SEO services matter more now, not less, because AI answers are assembled from pages that already rank. Google's AI Overviews draw on the same web index as normal results, so an organic ranking is the entry ticket to being cited. Clicks per query have compressed, which makes intent quality and brand demand worth more than raw traffic.
takeaways: There is no separate AI ranking pipeline. The retrieval layer feeding AI answers is the same index you've been optimising for.
Pew Research Center measured a real click drop: **8%** of visits with an AI summary produced a click on a result, versus **15%** without one.
What survived the compression is **intent-heavy and branded** search. What got hollowed out is definitional, top-of-funnel content.
Paid media's cost per lead resets to zero progress every month. SEO's doesn't — that gap widens, it doesn't close.
If your report still leads with sessions, it will read as failure in a year where impressions rise and clicks flatten.

sections.h2: The answer moved. The index didn't.
body: Here's the mechanic that most of the panic skips over. When Google generates an AI Overview, it isn't consulting a separate, secret pool of AI-approved content. It retrieves from the same web index that produces the ten blue links, applies broadly the same quality and relevance signals, then writes a summary over the top with citations attached.

That has one consequence worth more than every other take on the subject: **the pages that get cited are, overwhelmingly, pages that were already ranking** for the query or something adjacent to it. Being crawlable, being indexed, being genuinely useful on the query and having enough external corroboration to be trusted — the entry requirements didn't change. The layout on top of them did.

So the honest framing isn't "SEO is dead, learn GEO". It's that ranking became necessary but less sufficient. You still have to do the ranking part. You just can't stop there. [What Google AI Overviews are](/answers/what-are-google-ai-overviews) covers the mechanics in more detail.

callout.title: The uncomfortable corollary
callout.body: Every agency selling you a separate "AI optimisation" retainer on top of your SEO retainer is selling you the same crawl, the same content quality bar and the same authority work, invoiced twice. Ask them to name one tactic that only applies to AI answers and doesn't also help you rank.

sections.h2: The click compression, with the actual numbers
body: Two pieces of published research are worth knowing, and both deserve their caveats stated out loud.

**Pew Research Center**, publishing in July 2025 from browsing data collected in March 2025, found that when an AI summary appeared, users clicked a traditional search result on 8% of visits — against 15% of visits where no AI summary appeared. Roughly half the click rate. They also found that around 1% of visits produced a click on a source link inside the summary itself, which tells you the citation is a credibility signal far more than a traffic source.
**Ahrefs** published its own analysis in 2025 reporting a substantial average click-through-rate drop for the top-ranking page on queries where an AI Overview appears — in the region of a third.

Both studies are directional rather than universal. Pew's panel is US adults, the sample is modest, and search behaviour in India differs on device mix, language and query length. Ahrefs' data skews to the keyword sets its customers track, which are not a random sample of the web. Treat them as evidence that the effect is real and material, not as a coefficient you can apply to your own traffic.
Google has said publicly that clicks arriving via AI Overviews are higher quality. It has not published data supporting that. Weigh it accordingly.

callout.title: Don't extrapolate someone else's drop onto your site
callout.body: The compression is heavily query-dependent. A site whose traffic is 80% definitional queries and a site whose traffic is 80% branded and commercial queries live in different worlds. Segment your own Search Console data before you conclude anything.

sections.h2: What got hollowed out, and what barely moved
body: The loss isn't spread evenly, and understanding the pattern is what turns this from a scary headline into a plan.

bullets: If your content strategy was built on definitional top-of-funnel volume, the ground genuinely shifted under you.
If it was built on the queries people type with a credit card nearby, you lost far less than the headlines suggest.
The strategic move is not "write more". It's to shift the centre of gravity of what you publish down the funnel.

sections.h2: Branded demand became the asymmetry that decides everything
body: Branded search is the one query class no summary can take from you. When somebody types your company name, they've already chosen to evaluate you, and no AI answer talks them out of the click.

This creates an asymmetry that's been quietly widening. A brand people already know gets cited more often (familiarity and corroboration across the web are both signals), gets clicked more often when cited, and converts better when clicked. A brand nobody knows gets summarised and skipped.

Which means the SEO work that pays best now is the work that also builds recognition: original data nobody else has, named authors with real credentials, opinions that can be quoted, and being present in the places your category gets discussed. That's a meaningful shift from the old model of covering every keyword permutation and waiting.
The practical test: track your monthly branded search volume as a demand indicator. If unbranded clicks fall but branded searches climb, the channel is working and your dashboard is lying to you.

body: Set the AI question aside for a moment. There's a structural difference between organic and paid that's been true for twenty years and gets more pronounced as ad auctions get more crowded.

callout.title: This is not an argument against paid
callout.body: Run both. Paid buys you speed and a testing ground for messaging; organic buys you a cost base that improves. The mistake isn't choosing one — it's funding paid from cash flow and organic from whatever's left, which guarantees organic never compounds. Our [performance marketing](/performance) and [SEO](/seo) engagements are deliberately priced to run side by side.

sections.h2: What has to change in how you report this
body: Most SEO reporting was designed for a world where an impression reliably produced a click at a known rate. That relationship broke, and reports that ignore it will show failure where there is none — or hide failure where there is.
Five adjustments, in rough order of urgency:
numbered: **Stop leading with sessions.** Lead with qualified leads from organic, tracked in your CRM. Everything else is an intermediate variable.

**Read impressions and clicks as two separate stories.** Rising impressions with flat clicks used to mean a CTR problem. Now it can also mean your page is being read inside an answer box. Both are possible; find out which before you rewrite your title tags.

**Segment CTR by query type**, not sitewide. As things stand, Search Console folds AI Overview appearances into the same impression and click counts, so you cannot cleanly split them in the interface. Segmenting by definitional versus commercial queries is the closest honest proxy.
**Track branded search volume monthly.** It's the cleanest available read on whether the work is building demand rather than just harvesting it.

**Sample your citations manually.** Take your twenty most valuable queries, run them through the assistants your buyers use, and log whether you appear. The tooling for this is immature and mostly overpromises; a spreadsheet and forty minutes a month beats a dashboard that guesses. [Generative engine optimisation](/answers/what-is-generative-engine-optimization) covers what's real here and what isn't.

callout.title: The reporting trap
callout.body: An agency whose report still opens with a traffic graph in 2026 either hasn't noticed what changed or is counting on you not noticing. Ask what your organic qualified lead count was on day one. If nobody wrote it down, nobody can prove anything either way.

faqs.q: Is SEO still worth it now that AI answers most questions?
faqs.a: For commercial and branded queries, yes — those barely moved, and they're where the money is. For definitional top-of-funnel content, the return has genuinely fallen. The channel isn't dead; the cheapest tier of it is. If your whole plan was "what is X" articles, the plan needs rewriting, not the channel.

faqs.q: How do I get my pages cited in AI answers?
faqs.a: Rank first — citations overwhelmingly come from pages already performing in organic results. Then make the page easy to extract from: a direct answer near the top, clear structure, specific numbers, named authors, and claims that are corroborated elsewhere on the web. There is no separate submission route.

faqs.q: Should I block AI crawlers to protect my content?
faqs.a: Consider it carefully, because you can't be cited in a system that can't read you. Blocking makes sense if your business model is the content itself — a paywall, a data product. If your content exists to generate enquiries, blocking removes you from the surface where your buyers are increasingly starting.

faqs.q: Why are SEO services important for a small business specifically?
faqs.a: Because a small business can win narrow, specific queries that no large competitor bothers to target, and those queries convert far better than broad ones. The compression hit generic informational content hardest — which is exactly the content small businesses were never going to win anyway.

faqs.a: Retainers commonly run ₹25,000 to ₹3,00,000 a month depending on site size, competition and how much technical debt you're carrying. Our SEO starts at ₹75,000/mo, with smaller sites from ₹40,000, ex-GST. Below about ₹25,000 you're funding part-time attention rather than a team.
